evidence_items.locator: Section 3, fine-tuning with question-answer pairs; Figures 3 and 5a
evidence_items.explanation: GPT-3 fine-tuning experiments found strong performance within the training splits and poor generalization beyond them; multiplication was one of the tested tasks. This supports the proposed mechanism in a specific setting, but does not establish the pretraining coverage or causes of errors across contemporary LLMs.

Adding a small number of long examples enabled specialized transformers to generalize from shorter multiplication training to much longer operands. This supports the relevance of training coverage while showing that exhaustive sampling is unnecessary; it limits an interpretation that unsampled products inevitably cause failure.

The caption documents frequent last-digit errors by Llama 2 models on a multiplication example; duplicated digits reflect the page's mathematical rendering. The wider experiments find improved predictions when correct preceding digits are supplied, supporting the error observation while leaving training-outlier causation unestablished.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not document the relevant pretraining coverage of representative general-purpose LLMs well enough to identify the tested large products as training-distribution outliers.
Controlled fine-tuning failures support a narrower generalization problem, but do not isolate how much of ordinary LLM multiplication failure it explains.
Sparse-example generalization and sensitivity to generated answer prefixes prevent inferring the full causal claim from declining accuracy alone.
